title: Meaning & Evidence
description: Definition of fasting linguistically and technically, and the evidence for its obligation.
content_markdown:
## Meaning of Fasting

Linguistically, **Fasting (As-Shiyam)** means *Al-Imsak* (الإمساك), which is to withhold oneself from something, whether it be speech, food, or walking.

Technically (in Sharia), fasting is:

> **Worshipping Allah Ta'ala by withholding oneself from food, drink, sexual desires, and other invalidators, from the rising of the true dawn (Subuh) until the setting of the sun (Maghrib).**

## Evidence of Obligation

Ramadan fasting is the fourth pillar of Islam and its ruling is **Fardhu 'Ain** (obligatory for every individual). Allah Ta'ala says:

> يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
> 
> "O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous."
> (QS. Al-Baqarah: 183)

The Prophet ﷺ said:

> بُنِيَ الْإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ ... وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ
> "Islam is built upon five...
> [and mentioned] fasting Ramadan."
> (HR. Bukhari & Muslim)

## Levels of Fasting
Imam Al-Ghazali in *Ihya' Ulumuddin* divides fasting into three levels:
1.  **General Fasting**: Restraining the stomach and private parts from desires.
2.  **Special Fasting**: Restraining the hearing, sight, tongue, hands, and feet from all sins.
3.  **Special of the Special Fasting**: Restraining the heart from worldly desires and everything other than Allah.

title: Virtues of Fasting
description: Extraordinary virtues for those who fast and their rewards.
content_markdown:
## 1. Unlimited Reward
In a Hadith Qudsi, Allah Ta'ala says:

> كُلُّ عَمَلِ ابْنِ آدَمَ لَهُ إِلَّا الصِّيَامَ فَإِنَّهُ لِي وَأَنَا أَجْزِي بِهِ
> 
> "Every deed of the son of Adam is for him (multiplied 10 to 700 times), **except fasting**. For it is for Me and I will reward it directly."
> (HR. Bukhari & Muslim)

## 2. Fragrant Breath
The Prophet ﷺ said:

> وَلَخُلُوفُ فَمِ الصَّائِمِ أَطْيَبُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ رِيحِ الْمِسْكِ
> "Indeed, the smell of the mouth of a fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk."

## 3. Two Joys

> لِلصَّائِمِ فَرْحَتَانِ: فَرْحَةٌ عِنْدَ فِطْرِهِ، وَفَرْحَةٌ عِنْدَ لِقَاءِ رَبِّهِ
> "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord."

## 4. The Gate of Ar-Rayyan
Paradise has eight gates, one of which is called **Ar-Rayyan**. This gate is exclusively for those who fast. After they enter, it is closed and no one else enters through it.

## 5. Answered Prayers

> ثَلَاثَةٌ لَا تُرَدُّ دَعْوَتُهُمْ ... وَالصَّائِمُ حَتَّى يُفْطِرَ
> "Three people whose supplication is not rejected... [one of them is] the fasting person until he breaks his fast."
> (HR. Tirmidzi & Ibnu Majah)

title: Wisdoms of Fasting
description: Spiritual, social, and health benefits behind the fasting legislation.
content_markdown:
## Spiritual Wisdom
1.  **Achieving Taqwa**: Consistent with the main goal of fasting (La'allakum tattaqun), fasting trains absolute obedience to Allah's commands.
2.  **Training Patience**: Fasting combines three types of patience: patience in obedience, patience in refraining from sin, and patience in enduring pain (hunger/thirst).
3.  **Curbing Desires**: Fasting narrows the path of Satan flowing in human blood, making desires more controllable.

## Social Wisdom
1.  **Empathy for the Poor**: Hunger reminds us of the suffering of brothers and sisters who lack daily food.
2.  **Fostering Generosity**: The month of Ramadan is a month of charity and sharing (Iftar).

## Health Wisdom
1.  **Detoxification**: Resting the digestive system gives the body a chance to remove toxins.
2.  **Body Balance**: Helps lower blood sugar, cholesterol, and blood pressure.

title: Conditions
description: Difference between Obligatory Conditions and Validity Conditions.
content_markdown:
## Conditions for Obligation (Wajib)
If someone meets these criteria, they appear **sinful** if they abandon fasting:

1.  **Islam**: Disbelievers are not obliged to fast (in this world), but will be punished in the Hereafter for abandoning obligations.
2.  **Puberty (Baligh)**: Reached adulthood (marked by wet dreams or menstruation). Children are not obliged, but encouraged to practice.
3.  **Sanity ('Aql)**: The insane are not obliged to fast and are not sinful.
4.  **Ability (Qudrah)**: The severely sick or very elderly are not obliged to fast (replaced by Fidyah).
5.  **Resident (Mukim)**: Travelers (Musafir) may break their fast, but must make it up (Qadha).

## Conditions for Validity (Sah)
For fasting to be accepted by Allah, it must meet:

1.  **Islam**: Apostasy invalidates fasting.
2.  **Sanity** / **Discernment (Tamyiz)**: A child who has not reached the age of discernment (does not understand) is not valid in fasting.
3.  **Pure from Haid & Nifas**: Menstruating/postpartum women are forbidden to fast and their fasting is invalid.
4.  **Intention (Niyyah)**: Making intention at night before dawn.

> **Note**: If an obligatory condition is lost (e.g., going insane at noon), the obligation drops. If a validity condition is lost (e.g., menstruating at noon), the fasting is invalidated.

title: Pillars & Times
description: Pillars that must be fulfilled and fasting time limits.
content_markdown:
## 1. Intention (An-Niyyah)
Intention is the resolution of the heart to perform worship.
*   **Time of Intention**: For Obligatory Fasting (Ramadan, Qadha, Kaffarah), intention **must** be made at night (before Dawn).
*   The Prophet ﷺ said:
    > مَنْ لَمْ يُبَيِّتِ الصِّيَامَ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ فَلَا صِيَامَ لَهُ
    > "Whoever does not resolve to fast before dawn, there is no fast for him."

*   **For Voluntary Fasting**: It is permissible to make intention in the morning (before Dhuhr) as long as one has not eaten/drunk anything.

## 2. Abstaining (Al-Imsak)
Refraining from all invalidators (eating, drinking, intercourse, etc.) with the intention of worship.

## 3. Time Frame
*   **Start**: Rising of the True Dawn (Subuh).
    *   *Caution*: Imsak (10 minutes before Subuh) is just a precautionary time, not the forbidden limit. The limit is the Adhan of Subuh.
*   **End**: Perfect setting of the Sun (Maghrib).

title: Sunnahs of Fasting
description: Recommended acts to perfect the reward of fasting.
content_markdown:
## Sunnahs of Sahur
1.  **Eating Sahur**: "Eat Sahur, for indeed there is blessing in it." (HR. Bukhari)
2.  **Delaying Sahur**: It is recommended to eat Sahur close to the time of Subuh. The gap between the Prophet's ﷺ Sahur and prayer was about reading 50 verses.

## Sunnahs of Iftar (Breaking Fast)
1.  **Hastening Iftar (Ta'jiil)**: Break the fast immediately once the sun has set (Maghrib Adhan).
2.  **Order of Food**: Ruthab (wet dates) ➔ Tamr (dry dates) ➔ Water.
3.  **Supplication after Iftar**: 
    > ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَثَبَتَ الْأَجْرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
    > "The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills."
    (HR. Abu Daud - Hasan)

## Other Sunnahs
*   **Reading Al-Qur'an**: Tadarus (reading & studying).
*   **Feeding the Fasting (Iftar)**: The reward is the same as the fasting person without diminishing their reward.
*   **Charity (Sadaqah)**: The Prophet ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was even more generous in Ramadan.
*   **I'tikaf**: Secluding oneself in the mosque during the last 10 days of Ramadan.

title: Invalidators
description: Things that invalidate fasting and their consequences.
content_markdown:
## 1. Eating & Drinking Intentionally
Including inserting objects into the body through the mouth or nose.
*   If eating/drinking out of **Forgetfulness**, the fast is **NOT invalidated** and may be continued.

## 2. Sexual Intercourse (Jima')
Having sexual relations during the day of Ramadan is a major sin.
*   **Consequence**: Fast invalidated, must make up (Qadha), and must pay **Major Expiation (Kaffarah Mughallazah)**: 
    1. Freeing a slave, if unable then:
    2. Fasting 2 consecutive months, if unable then:
    3. Feeding 60 poor people.

## 3. Vomiting Intentionally
Inserting a finger into the throat or other means to induce vomiting.
*   If vomiting is **unintentional** (due to illness/nausea), the fast is **NOT invalidated**.

## 4. Menstruation & Postpartum Bleeding
A woman who bleeds due to Haid or Nifas, even a moment before Maghrib, her fast is invalid and must be made up.

## 5. Nutritious Injections (IV Drips)
Injections containing nutritional replacements invalidate fasting. As for medicinal injections (painkillers, vaccines) that do not nourish, the strongest opinion is that they do not invalidate.

## 6. Ejaculation Intentionally
Due to masturbation or intimacy (skin contact). If solely due to a wet dream, the fast is not invalidated.

title: Permitted Acts
description: Acts that are allowed and often misunderstood.
content_markdown:
## Permissible Acts (Mubah)

1.  **Bathing & Pouring Water over Head**: To refresh the body from heat or thirst.
2.  **Rinsing Mouth & Nose**: Permitted during Wudu, provided it is not excessive.
3.  **Siwak / Brushing Teeth**: Permitted in the morning or afternoon. Be careful not to swallow toothpaste.
4.  **Tasting Food**: For the cook, it is allowed to taste on the tip of the tongue then **spit it out**, do not swallow.
5.  **Eye/Ear Drops**: Does not invalidate fasting according to the strong opinion, as it is not a passageway for food.
6.  **Bleeding from Wounds/Nosebleed**: Does not invalidate fasting. Cupping (Hijamah) has a difference of opinion (some say it invalidates).
7.  **Swallowing Saliva**: Saliva itself inside the mouth does not invalidate. As for **Phlegm**, it should be spat out.

title: Disliked Acts (Makruh)
description: Acts that should be avoided to maximize reward.
content_markdown:
## Disliked Acts

1.  **Exaggerating in Rinsing Mouth/Nose**: Because of the fear that water might reach the throat. The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Exaggerate in rinsing your nose unless you are fasting."*
2.  **Tasting Food without Need**: If there is no urgent need, it should be avoided.
3.  **Wishal Fasting**: Fasting for two consecutive days without breaking the fast at night. This is forbidden by the Prophet ﷺ.
4.  **Kissing/Embracing**: For those who cannot control their desires, as it may lead to invalidators (ejaculation/intercourse).
5.  **Obscene Speech & Useless Talk**: Backbiting, lying, gossiping, and dirty words do not invalidate fasting juristically, but **erase the reward of fasting**.
    > "How many fasting people get nothing from their fast except hunger and thirst." (HR. At-Tabarani)

title: Valid Excuses (Rukhshah)
description: Categories granted leniency and rules for Qadha/Fidyah.
content_markdown:
## 1. Obligatory Qadha (Making up later)
For those who break their fast due to a temporary excuse:
*   **The Sick**: Who has hope of recovery.
*   **The Traveler**: Who is on a journey (± 80km).
*   **Menstruating/Postpartum Women**: Obliged to make up fasting, not prayer.

## 2. Obligatory Fidyah (Paying Expiation)
For those unable to fast permanently:
*   **The Very Elderly**: Who are too weak to fast. Pay Fidyah of 1 mud (± 7 ounces of staple food) or feed one poor person for every day missed.
*   **Chronically Ill**: Severe illness with no hope of recovery according to medicine.

## 3. Pregnant & Breastfeeding Women
There is a difference of opinion among scholars. The precautionary opinion:
*   If she fears for **herself**, obligatory **Qadha**.
*   If she fears for **her fetus/baby**, obligatory **Qadha** (and some scholars add Fidyah).
*   The majority of scholars oblige Qadha for both cases.

title: Common Misconceptions
description: Clarifying misunderstandings about fasting in society.
content_markdown:
## 1. Imsak Time
Many think the "Imsak" mark on the schedule (10 minutes before Subuh) means eating is forbidden. In fact, it is only a time of *precaution* so we can get ready. The limit for forbidden eating is at **Adhan Subuh (True Dawn)**.

## 2. Sleeping of a Fasting Person is Worship
The Hadith *"The sleep of a fasting person is worship"* is **WEAK (Dhaif)** or even Fabricated according to some Hadith scholars. Sleep can be worship if intended to gather strength for worship, but if sleeping out of laziness, it is blameworthy.

## 3. Breaking Fast with Sweets
There is no Hadith *"Break your fast with something sweet"*. The Sunnah is to break fast with **Ruthab** or **Tamr** (Dates). If not available, then Water. Sweet foods (kolak, sweet tea) are permissible, but not the main Sunnah.

## 4. Forgetting to Eat Invalidates Fast
If one truly forgets, their fast is still valid and not invalidated; it is considered a provision from Allah. Stop eating immediately when remembering.
